text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: high runtime CPU 95th >85% in cluster runtime-eu-west-1 — alert_id=PD-66721 — severity: P1 — runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/runtime-cpu|runtime-cpu>
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-66721 created by alertmanager. Trigger: node/runtime-gpu-12 (avg 95th CPU 89%). Recent symptoms: latency spikes, 5xx rate steady. PagerDuty escalation policy: oncall-sre -> eng-lead.
maya: ACK — I'm oncall, looking now. Starting quick triage.
maya: quick checks:
```
# check node CPU and pods
kubectl top node runtime-gpu-12
kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep runtime-service
kubectl logs -n runtime runtime-service-5ff7c -c runtime | tail -n 80
```
maya: logs show a flurry of heavy attention ops on a single pod, lots of `kv-cache` warmup spikes and repeated large prefix loads around the same timestamp window. Not seeing higher 5xx rate in the API gateway.
liam: pinging infra to confirm no noisy batch jobs? @andre any infra scheduled jobs in that window?
andre: nope, nothing scheduled. I see a spike in concurrent modelLoads from a single customer session (session-id truncated). Could be a runaway client or a misrouted traffic burst.
maya: trying a rolling restart of the pod to clear cache state, will keep it canary (one pod) and monitor.
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-service -n runtime --selector=pool=eu-west
```
maya: did restart one replica; CPU on node dropped from 89% -> 46% within ~40s.
incident-bot: Alertmanager auto-resolved alert PD-66721 (threshold cleared). Auto-resolve reason: CPU 95th < configured threshold for 3m.
maya: marking as acknowledged -> resolved. No customer-facing errors observed (no increase in 5xx). Monitoring shows latency returned to baseline within 2m. :white_check_mark:
sasha: nice, thanks. Was this an alert flapping or a one-off spike we should suppress?
liam: looks transient but likely caused by an outlier client flood + cold KV warmup. Suggest we add a short-lived suppression for node-level CPU alerts during known warmup windows and also tune alert threshold or add a rate-of-change condition to avoid single-spike PD noise.
andre: proposed Alertmanager rule change (draft):
```
- alert: RuntimeNodeHighCPU
  expr: node_cpu_seconds_total:rate5m > 0.85
  for: 5m
  annotations:
    summary: "High CPU on runtime node"
  labels:
    severity: page
```
Change: increase `for` to 10m or add `unless` clause for `kv_warmup_active` metric.
sasha: can we add a short suppression that auto-applies when `kv_warmup_active > 0.5`? That would stop the PD echoes during expected warmups.
maya: filed a follow-up ticket: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-4321 — description: "Investigate transient node CPU spikes from per-session modelLoads + add alert suppression / rate-of-change guard". Assignee: liam.
oncall-rota: noting handoff: I'll be oncall in ~2.5h; leaving the thread — no further immediate action needed unless PD pages again. Please update runbook section "cpu-flap-mitigation" with the suppression advice.
liam: will take ticket and update runbook. Also will add a short note in postmortem queue if we see >3 repeats in 24h.
maya: quick customer-impact check: zero customer-90th latency regressions and no support tickets in the window. Marking incident as no-customer-impact.
sasha: thumbs up. Actions: (1) liam to adjust rule/detect warmup condition; (2) add brief suppression in Alertmanager; (3) add runbook note; (4) monitor for repeat. I'll set a dashboard alert for repeat counts per 24h.
andre: adding correlation to request-id logs for that session so we can trace it next time. If this repeats we'll throttle that session upstream.
incident-bot: Closing thread (auto-resolve recorded). If PD pages again within 30m, it'll re-open under same incident.
maya: thanks all. low-severity close. :v:
